articles.title: Compulsory database ‘must be tough on rogue landlords’ says lettings boss
articles.summary: The Lettings Industry Council chief speaks out
articles.ai_summary:
- The head of the Lettings Industry Council advocates for a stringent compulsory database to crack down on rogue landlords.  
- Stronger measures are essential to protect tenants and promote accountability in the rental market.

articles.title: Right to have pets has had little impact so far – claim
articles.summary: Very few landlords appear to have had a request to keep a pet
articles.ai_summary:
- New regulations allowing tenants to request pets in rental properties have seen minimal uptake, with few landlords receiving such requests.  
- The anticipated impact of pet-friendly policies on the rental market has yet to materialize, raising questions about tenant demand for pet ownership.

articles.title: Build To Rent in crisis as starts plummet by 79%
articles.summary: New figures from Savills set alarm bells ringing
articles.ai_summary:
- Build To Rent projects have seen a staggering 79% drop in starts, raising concerns within the property sector.  
- Savills warns that the significant decline could signal a looming crisis in the UK rental market.

articles.title: Tenants complain that landlords make it hard to charge electric cars
articles.summary: Even so, most renters say EV charging is easy
articles.ai_summary:
- Tenants are facing challenges from landlords regarding the installation of electric vehicle (EV) charging points.  
- Despite these hurdles, a majority of renters still find EV charging to be straightforward.

articles.title: Landlord ignores Improvement Notice and ends up in court

articles.ai_summary:
- A landlord faced legal action after disregarding an Improvement Notice, leading to a court appearance.  
- He was ordered to pay a total of over £6,400 in penalties.

articles.title: Possessions already changing because of Section 21 ending

articles.ai_summary:

- Insights from Paul Shamplina and Landlord Action reveal that landlords are adapting their strategies in response to these legislative changes.

articles.title: Monthly rent up again despite market volatility easing
articles.summary: This is the latest data from HomeLet
articles.ai_summary:

articles.title: Government backs massive institutional rental scheme

articles.ai_summary:

articles.title: High Court decision means landlord licensing will go ahead
articles.summary: The High Court has for the second time  dismissed a judicial review of Thurrock council’s Selective Licensing Scheme. The claimant had sought an oral hearing to challenge the High Court’s previous written decision to dismiss the claim on March 13 this year.  That decision allowed the authority to start to implement the scheme. The court has […]
articles.ai_summary:
- The High Court has upheld Thurrock council’s Selective Licensing Scheme, dismissing a second judicial review attempt.
- This ruling clears the way for the council to move forward with implementing the landlord licensing initiative.

articles.title: Renters Rights Act triggers changed tenant behaviour, says agent
articles.summary: Tenants are increasingly discerning, claims the agent
